findings.claim: An oversized first event can produce an empty page with `has_more=true`, causing MCP clients to loop forever with an unchanged `nextAfter` cursor.
findings.evidence: The added `events_page_after` returns `Ok((events, true))` when `response_bytes.saturating_add(encoded_bytes) > max_bytes` before pushing the event; if `events` is empty, `crates/prometheus-exec/src/mcp.rs` computes `next_after = events.last().map_or(after, |event| event.sequence)`, so the caller receives no events, `hasMore: true`, and the same exclusive cursor. This violates the documented continuation contract in `site/docs/execution/local-api-cli-and-mcp.md`: `Pass the returned exclusive nextAfter cursor as the next call's after; hasMore indicates that another page is available.`
findings.suggested_fix: If the next event alone exceeds the byte budget, return an explicit error instead of an empty `has_more` page, or otherwise guarantee cursor progress without silently skipping the event.
